subject: Subprocessor annex and country transfer snapshot request
messages:
From: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@evergreenbank.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@evergreenbank.com>, legal <legal@evergreenbank.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Subprocessor annex + country transfer summary request

Hi Naomi / Kimberly —

Thanks for the chat yesterday. Legal and procurement asked me to collect the following before we can move to an internal review: 

1) A current subprocessor annex (all subprocessors, roles, and contractual tier) that we can attach to the DPA addendum.
2) A per-country transfer summary that lists where data may transit or be stored (by processor), and the export jurisdictions for each subprocessor.
3) For EU / UK controlled data, confirmation of onshore fallback options (if the primary processor routes outside the UK/EU), and whether there are any planned changes in the next 6 months.
4) KMS/HSM jurisdiction for any subprocessors handling encryption keys and whether keys are customer-managed.
5) SOC 2 / ISO references and where we can pull evidence (links or packaged PDF).

Target: procurement would like to complete the commercial review by Dec 10 — can you confirm if you can provide the annex and the country snapshot by EOD Dec 4 PST? If not, let us know the soonest delivery date.

Thanks,
Amelia Torres
Senior Sourcing Manager, Evergreen Bank
amelia.torres@evergreenbank.com
Attachments: none
From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-04T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor annex + country transfer summary request

Amelia —

Appreciate the clear list. We can get you a compiled annex and a per-country snapshot today. Quick clarifying questions so we include the right level of detail: 

- Do you need IP addresses / ASN-level egress detail or is country / region-level mapping sufficient for procurement?
- Should we include temporary/ephemeral subprocessors (e.g., short-term analytics bridges) in the annex, or only long-lived contracted processors?

Tentative plan: I will attach "Subprocessor_Annex_v3.pdf" with full roster and contractual tier, and a separate spreadsheet "Country_Transfer_Snapshot_Evergreen.xlsx" that maps processor -> country of processing/transit -> export jurisdiction -> KMS jurisdiction -> SOC2 reference.

Marissa will own the SOC2/attestation links and certification copies. Kimberly — can you confirm whether we should push a DPA addendum draft to DocuSign now or wait until procurement completes the review?

We aim to have the annex + snapshot to you by 4:30pm PST today.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Subprocessor annex + country transfer summary request

Amelia —

Thanks — a couple of legal asks so we can triage risk quickly: 

- Please confirm whether Evergreen will accept our standard DPA addendum (we typically use an annex that lists subprocessors + a short exportability clause). If not, we can stand up a redline.
- For EU/UK data: procurement expects an explicit onshore fallback statement for critical telemetry and logging. Naomi — please include a separate tab in the spreadsheet that shows fallback vendors and any onshore-only routing we can guarantee.
- If Evergreen requires customer-managed keys for specific data classes, note that our platform supports Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private customers — we'll include KMS jurisdiction information.

I have attached a procurement-friendly country snapshot template we frequently send to banks — filled partially by Marissa. Also linking the HubSpot record for deal context: https://redwood.app.link/hubspot/DEAL-4821 

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Subprocessor annex + country transfer summary request — annex and snapshot attached

Hi Amelia —

Attached are the items requested: 

1) Subprocessor_Annex_v3.pdf — current roster (includes contracted + transient processors we rely on for telemetry and analytics). Each entry includes: role, primary location, export jurisdictions, contract tier, and whether encryption keys are customer-managed.
2) Country_Transfer_Snapshot_Evergreen.xlsx — per-country mapping with an additional tab for EU/UK onshore fallback options and expected time-to-failover in the event a primary processor is blocked.

Quick summary (high-level):
- No planned changes to critical subprocessors in the next 3 months. Any non-critical temporary analytics bridges are flagged in the annex and have their own retention/escrow commitments.
- KMS: For hosted customers, Redwood manages keys in the US by default; Dedicated/Private customers can BYOK and keep keys in customer-chosen regions. The annex marks which processors touch plaintext and whether keys are customer-managed.
- Evidence: SOC2 reports for the major processors (LogStream, EdgeBridge, KeyVaultCo) are linked in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example

Next steps: 
- If Evergreen is happy with the annex and snapshot, Kimberly — please confirm if you want us to send the DPA addendum to DocuSign now (DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/embedded/?r=example-id-123).
- Amelia — happy to do a 30-min walkthrough tomorrow morning PST to step through any items procurement flags.
